title: Larynx and trachea (anterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Location
Front of the neck at the level of C3, between the mandible and the larynx. It is U-shaped.
Articulates with
No other bone. It is held in place by muscles and ligaments, with the thyrohyoid membrane joining it to the larynx.
Features
Body with greater and lesser horns. It anchors the tongue and the suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles.
hy: A fractured hyoid in an adult is associated with strangulation, but it is not proof of it by itself.

rows: Location
Leaf-shaped elastic cartilage behind the root of the tongue and the hyoid bone, attached by its stalk to the inside of the thyroid cartilage.
Function
Folds back over the entrance to the larynx during swallowing and keeps food out of the airway.
hy: Epiglottitis, classically due to Haemophilus influenzae type b in an unvaccinated child, causes fever, drooling and noisy breathing; a swollen epiglottis shows as a thumbprint on a lateral X-ray of the neck.

rows: Location
Largest cartilage of the larynx, at the level of C4 to C5. Its two plates meet in front at the laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple).
Function
Shields the front of the larynx. The vocal ligaments attach to the back of the angle between its plates, and its inferior horns hinge on the cricoid cartilage.
Location
Below the thyroid cartilage at the level of C6, where the larynx becomes the trachea and the pharynx becomes the esophagus. It is shaped like a signet ring, narrow in front and tall behind.
Function
Forms the base of the larynx and carries the arytenoid cartilages. It is the only complete ring of cartilage in the airway.
Location
Runs from the cricoid cartilage at C6 to its division into the two main bronchi at the level of the sternal angle. The esophagus lies behind it.
Function
Carries air to and from the lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage hold it open, and the gap at the back is closed by the trachealis muscle.
hy: In the most common form of tracheoesophageal fistula the upper esophagus ends blindly and the lower esophagus opens into the trachea; the newborn drools, chokes and turns blue with the first feed.

rows: Attachments
Upper border of the thyroid cartilage to the body of the hyoid bone. It is the thickened midline part of the thyrohyoid membrane.
Function
Hangs the larynx from the hyoid bone.
Attachments
Lower border of the thyroid cartilage to the arch of the cricoid cartilage, in the midline. It is the front of the cricothyroid membrane.
Function
Joins the thyroid and cricoid cartilages at the front of the larynx.
hy: The site of an emergency cricothyrotomy: the airway is opened here, below the vocal folds.

rows: Origin
Anterolateral surface of the cricoid cartilage.
Insertion
Inferior border and inferior horn of the thyroid cartilage.
Innervation
External branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (from the vagus).
Action
Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward, which lengthens and tightens the vocal folds and raises the pitch of the voice.
hy: The only intrinsic muscle of the larynx not supplied by the recurrent laryngeal nerve. Its nerve runs with the superior thyroid artery and is at risk in thyroidectomy.
